task.description:
WF-03 Step 1 diagnosis + exact fix design (ISSUE-FIXER, .claude/agents/issue-fixer.md) for Q-1054 / GH #2400, queue issue_ref ISS-1054 (R1, MEDIUM, ISS-1042 follow-up, SECURITY-REVIEWER F2). Branch feature/WF03-ISS1054DBGUARD-20261012. NOTE ID collision: the local file docs/issues/ISS-1059.yaml is an already-resolved record (Q-1038) while the queue now also has an issue ref ISS-1059 (a different follow-up); pick the next FREE local ISS id by checking docs/issues AND `git ls-remote`/origin branches AND the queue (GET https://queue-test.ai-dala.com/tasks?status=open with header Authorization: Bearer <QUEUE_AUTH_TOKEN from ./.env, parse with grep/cut>) for ISS-10xx, create docs/issues/<id>.yaml for this issue with queue_ref Q-1054, github_ref GH-2400 (follow the schema of docs/issues/ISS-1058.yaml), and report the id.

Problem: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex `start_pool!/2` (line ~382) and the pool worker `Letflow.TenantFixture.Pool` reset/truncate tenant-schema rows between tests (dirty-table reset, rebuild, final guard reset, teardown drop of slot schemas and Registration/Tenant rows). If the pool is ever pointed at a database that is not the test database, those resets/drops could destroy real data. Acceptance: (1) start_pool!/2 checks `SELECT current_database()` against the configured test database (derive the expected name from Letflow.Repo config / the test config, do not hard-code) and raises BEFORE it provisions, clones or resets anything; (2) a test asserts the refusal when the name does not match; (3) a mutation (removing the guard) makes the refusal test fail; (4) no change to reset semantics when the guard passes.

Do: read test/support/tenant_fixture.ex fully (start_pool!/2, create_slots, the Pool GenServer, teardown, and also every other path that drops/truncates: pool_teardown!, recycle_pool!, rebuild, final guard) and decide the minimal correct placement: the guard must precede the first side effect (Sandbox.mode(:auto) is fine; GenServer.start of the worker and create_slots are not) and, if the worker has independent entry points that destructively act, whether a second assertion belongs in the worker's init. Decide how to make the refusal TESTABLE without pointing at a real non-test DB: e.g. an injectable/overridable expected-name via opts (`:expected_database`) or a private function seam, kept test-support only; the default must be the real configured test DB. Check how existing tests for the pool (test/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs or similar; grep) are structured (async: false, one pool per module per VM) so the new refusal test does not leak a registered pool or break siblings. Check docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md and docs/anti-patterns.md for anything relevant. Deliver the exact design (function signatures, the SQL, error type/message, where the expected name comes from, the test list incl. a mutant list: M1 guard removed, M2 guard placed after create_slots, M3 compares wrong value), the exact files to touch (expected: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex + its test file + docs), and the risks. Do NOT write the implementation. No mix is needed (if you must run one, use the machine mutex: L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$L")"; until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 20; done; trap 'rmdir "$L" 2>/dev/null' EXIT; cd /c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow && LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test <ONE mix invocation>). Foreground only; no Monitors. Result into this handoff (COMPLETED, result.status PASS/FAIL, no BOM, LF; no self-reference in artifacts_out); pull --rebase, commit, push with bounded retry on github resolve failures; commit message ends 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'.

result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS (confirmed by reading every destructive path; no mix run needed): the hazard is real and unguarded. Letflow.TenantFixture.start_pool!/2 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex L382) calls Sandbox.mode(:auto), then GenServer.start(Letflow.TenantFixture.Pool, ...), then call_worker!(worker, {:create_slots, specs}). From there the worker issues destructive statements through Letflow.Repo with no check of which database it is connected to: teardown_slot (L2047: DELETE FROM public.<keyed>, DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS <slot> CASCADE, Repo.delete_all Registration and Tenant), reset_public!/restore_row!, reset (TRUNCATE of dirty tables), rebuild and final_guard!. The only DB identity query in the file is busy_backends (L2027, datname = current_database()), a lock probe, not a guard. The Repo database comes from config/test.exs L76 (letflow_test<MIX_TEST_PARTITION>); config/runtime.exs only overrides it with DATABASE_URL under config_env()==:prod. So a mis-pointed config, env/URL override or a runner copied against letflow_dev would run all of the above against real data with no refusal. All destructive entry points live in the worker, reachable via start_pool!/2: pool_teardown!/1 (L632, on_exit, worker :teardown), recycle_pool!/0, rebuild, final_guard!. Teardown's schema drop is the highest-blast-radius one. docs/anti-patterns.md and security-invariants.md contain nothing that conflicts (anti-patterns L2761-2790 is stale letflow_test* DBs, unrelated).

LOCAL ID: ISS-1061 (docs/issues has 1047-1052, 1058, 1059; queue holds ISS-1000..1060 across statuses; no origin branch or ref uses 1061). docs/issues/ISS-1061.yaml created with queue_ref Q-1054, github_ref GH-2400. The queue's own issue_ref for this task stays ISS-1054; use ISS-1061 in code comments, test describe and commit text and note the mapping.

EXACT FIX DESIGN (test-support only; no lib/ change; reset semantics untouched)

1. New public function in Letflow.TenantFixture (@doc false, called from the test file):
   @spec assert_test_database!(expected :: String.t() | nil) :: :ok
   def assert_test_database!(expected \\ nil) do
     expected = expected || Keyword.fetch!(Letflow.Repo.config(), :database)
     unless is_binary(expected) and String.starts_with?(expected, "letflow_test"), do: raise ArgumentError, "LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE phase=pool_database_guard expected database #{inspect(expected)} is not a letflow_test* database; refusing to provision, clone, reset or drop anything"
     %{rows: [[actual]]} = Letflow.Repo.query!("SELECT current_database()")
     if actual != expected, do: raise ArgumentError, "LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE phase=pool_database_guard connected to database #{inspect(actual)} but the configured test database is #{inspect(expected)}; refusing to provision, clone, reset or drop anything"
     :ok
   end
   Expected name source: Letflow.Repo.config()[:database] (the config/test.exs value incl. MIX_TEST_PARTITION), never a literal. The "letflow_test" prefix check is a second independent invariant on the effective expected name: comparing current_database() with Repo.config()[:database] alone is a tautology when the config itself is mis-pointed (config at letflow_dev). The prefix is the convention in config/test.exs L76 and scripts/test_parallel.sh (letflow_test<i>); CI creates letflow_dev only as the bootstrap DB. Error type ArgumentError (matches the other start_pool! rejections; setup_all failure aborts the module before anything exists). Two distinct message phrases so tests tell the branches apart: "is not a letflow_test* database" and "but the configured test database is".

2. start_pool!/2: new optional pool opt :expected_database (String.t(), test-support seam; default nil = configured DB; add to pool_opts type and docstring; NOT a slot-spec key, normalize_spec! untouched). Placement: after the existing side-effect-free argument validation and after `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` (needed so the query runs on an ordinary pool connection), strictly BEFORE GenServer.start, on_exit registration and create_slots:
     Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)
     :ok = assert_test_database!(Keyword.get(opts, :expected_database))
     init = %{module: ..., hooks: ..., parity_check: ..., expected_database: Keyword.get(opts, :expected_database)}
   Rationale: a raise after GenServer.start (M2) leaks a registered, never-torn-down worker (already_started for every later start in the VM); after create_slots the clones already exist. Raising before start leaves nothing to tear down, so no on_exit is needed.

3. Worker defense in depth: first statement of Letflow.TenantFixture.Pool.init/1 (L1299): `:ok = TenantFixture.assert_test_database!(Map.get(init, :expected_database))`. A raise in init makes GenServer.start return {:error, {exception, stacktrace}}, no process, no name registered; start_pool! cannot reach it after step 2 (same Repo just passed), so add no new case clause. Cost: one SELECT per pool per module. Pool is a public module and could be GenServer.start-ed without start_pool!/2. Do NOT add it to teardown/rebuild/reset/final_guard (db identity cannot change mid-run in one VM; per-statement checks are noise on a hot path).

4. No change to reset/rebuild/final_guard/teardown code, slot specs, defaults or public API shapes; with the guard passing behavior is identical (acceptance 4).

TESTS (test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs; module Letflow.Support.TenantFixturePoolTest is already async: false with one live pool; add describe "ISS-1061 database guard" there; no second module that starts a real pool is needed because refusal must not start one):
   T1 guard accepts the real DB: assert :ok == TenantFixture.assert_test_database!() and :ok == TenantFixture.assert_test_database!(Repo.config()[:database]) (acceptance 4, M3).
   T2 refusal on mismatch (acceptance 2): expected = "letflow_test_not_this_db" (has the prefix so it passes check one and reaches the comparison); assert_raise ArgumentError, ~r/but the configured test database is/; assert the message contains both the actual and the expected names.
   T3 non-test expected name refused before any query: assert_raise ArgumentError, ~r/is not a letflow_test\* database/, fn -> TenantFixture.assert_test_database!("letflow_dev") end (kills M6).
   T4 start_pool! refuses before any side effect (acceptance-critical): fresh = Module.concat(__MODULE__, "GuardRefusal#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"); snapshot `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant_%'` and count(*) of public.tenants; assert_raise ArgumentError, ~r/but the configured test database is/, fn -> TenantFixture.start_pool!(%{module: fresh, async: false}, slots: [@a], expected_database: "letflow_test_not_this_db") end; then assert Process.whereis(TenantFixture.pool_name(fresh)) == nil, both counts unchanged, and pool_stats(ctx.tenant_pool) of the live pool unchanged. Fresh module atom: no registry collision, nothing to clean up.
   T5 worker-level guard (kills M5): fresh2 likewise; assert {:error, {%ArgumentError{message: m}, _}} = GenServer.start(Letflow.TenantFixture.Pool, %{module: fresh2, expected_database: "letflow_test_not_this_db"}) with m =~ "but the configured test database is". Wrap in try/after that stops the pid if M5 yields {:ok, pid} so a mutant run does not leak.
   T6 default path unchanged: existing setup_all (no :expected_database) and the existing "async / unknown-async / empty / unknown-key / duplicate pools are rejected" test keep passing (guard runs after those validations; duplicate case passes the guard on the same DB).
   Verify: scoped `mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs` plus test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs under the machine mutex, one invocation each.

MUTANT LIST (each applied alone, must make the named test fail):
   M1 remove the assert_test_database! call from start_pool!/2: T4 fails (no raise; a pool is cloned under fresh); T5 still passes.
   M2 move the call to after GenServer.start or after create_slots: T4 fails (raise happens but whereis(pool_name(fresh)) != nil and schema/tenant counts moved).
   M3 compare the wrong value (e.g. current_database() vs Repo.config()[:username] or current_schema(), or expected vs itself): "always unequal" variant fails T1 (valid DB refused); "always equal" variant fails T2, T4, T5.
   M4 override ignored (expected replaced by Repo.config()[:database] unconditionally): T2, T4, T5 fail, T1 passes.
   M5 remove the Pool.init guard: T5 fails (GenServer.start returns {:ok, pid}).
   M6 remove the prefix check, keep only the equality check: T3 fails (message branch differs).
   M7 fail-open (Logger.warning instead of raise, or a non-ArgumentError): T2, T4, T5 fail.

FILES TO TOUCH: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (assert_test_database!/1, start_pool!/2 opt+call+init map, Pool.init first statement, pool_opts type, start_pool! doc paragraph, one sentence in Pool moduledoc); test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs (describe + T1..T5); docs/issues/ISS-1061.yaml (created now as open; resolve at the end); optionally one paragraph in lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md fail-closed section. No separate design artefact is needed given the size; ORCH can route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on this handoff then ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER. No lib/ change, so no tenant-data-path SECURITY-REVIEWER gate beyond awareness (only test fixtures change).

RISKS: (R1) The prefix check hard-codes "letflow_test", a convention not derived config; if a host/CI names its test DB differently the whole pooled suite refuses to start (loud, fail-closed, message names the cause). It is the only non-tautological part, so keep it; if ORCH prefers zero hard-coding, drop it plus T3/M6 and accept that the guard then only catches connection-vs-Repo.config divergence, not a mis-pointed config. (R2) Repo.config() is the runtime config after Repo.init/2 (lib/letflow/repo.ex L16); implementer must confirm init/2 does not rewrite :database (T1 would catch it). (R3) The query must run after Sandbox.mode(:auto); before it, DataCase can leave the mode at {:shared, dead_pid}. Keep the ordering in step 2. (R4) MIX_TEST_PARTITION=N gives letflow_testN; equality and prefix both pass. (R5) The :expected_database seam cannot be used to disarm the guard: a real non-test DB name is still stopped by the prefix check. (R6) ID collision: the queue has a second ISS-1059 and local ISS-1059.yaml belongs to Q-1038; this work uses local ISS-1061 while the queue ref stays ISS-1054; put the mapping in commit and PR text. (R7) T4's global pg_namespace and public.tenants count snapshots could race only with other writers on the same DB; partitions use separate letflow_test<i> DBs and the module is async: false; if flaky, assert only that no schema with the fresh module's prefix exists.
